questionText: What is the primary role of an Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC) in a microcontroller?
optionA: Converts continuous physical analog voltage into discrete digital values for CPU processing
optionB: Generates variable high-speed PWM pulses for motor driving
optionC: Amplifies microvolt-level audio signals directly to loudspeakers
optionD: Stores program machine instructions in non-volatile flash memory
explanation: An ADC samples continuous physical analog sensor signals (e.g. temperature or pressure) and quantizes them into digital binary values.

questionText: Which communication protocol uses two wires: Serial Data (SDA) and Serial Clock (SCL)?
explanation: I2C requires only two bidirectional open-drain lines: SDA (Serial Data) and SCL (Serial Clock) with pull-up resistors.

questionText: In microcontrollers what is the purpose of an Interrupt Service Routine (ISR)?
optionA: To compile C source code directly on the silicon core
optionB: To execute urgent asynchronous hardware events immediately when triggered
optionC: To continuously poll sensor pins in an infinite while loop
optionD: To manage file systems on external SD cards
explanation: An ISR is a specialized routine invoked immediately by hardware when an interrupt condition occurs pausing background execution.

questionText: What happens if a microcontroller port pin is configured as a floating input without pull-up or pull-down resistors?
optionA: The pin draws excessive current and burns the output transistor
optionB: The pin state can drift randomly between HIGH and LOW due to electromagnetic noise
optionC: The pin is permanently held at 5V logic HIGH
optionD: The microcontroller automatically triggers a hardware brownout reset
explanation: A floating high-impedance input has no defined voltage reference and easily drifts due to ambient electric fields causing indeterminate reads.

questionText: Which register in 8051 and AVR microcontrollers is typically used to set a pin direction as either INPUT or OUTPUT?
explanation: In AVR and standard MCUs the DDR (Data Direction Register) configures individual GPIO pins as either input (0) or output (1).
